comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

This is because 'vim-sandwich' [provides its own textobject for `is`](https://github.com/machakann/vim-sandwich?tab=readme-ov-file#textobj-sandwich), in the form of a dedicated mapping. In these type of conflicts a dedicated mapping takes precedence over a single `i` mapping that is used in 'mini.ai' to create its textobjects.

Described steps which include typing quickly and waiting result into different mappings being "activated" based on how Neovim interprets what user has pressed: if there is no key press within 'timeoutlen' milliseconds, then it considers current key sequence finished and executes it.

There is nothing 'mini.ai' can do here to avoid these type of conflicts apart from suggesting users to execute `:xmap i` and see if there are conflicting mappings.

In this particular case:
- Use different textobject identifier instead of `s`.
- Use 'mini.surround', which has same as 'vim-sandwich' default mappings, but no dedicated textobjects.

title: [mini.ai] conflict with vim-sandwich
